A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVGD convergence study. Their complete 26-page texts, equations, introductory schematic, references, and Appendices A.1–A.6 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports mathematical convergence theorems and proofs, including throughout Appendix A. No original experiments, simulations, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v4 likewise contains theoretical results and proofs, without original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The SVGD updates in Equations (1)–(2), step-size prescription in Equation (10), and bilinear-plus-Matérn kernels in Equations (11)–(12) are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets, simulated tasks, or empirical test scenarios. The illustrative classes of target distributions remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Comparisons with prior theoretical results, including Shi and Mackey (2024), are retained.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols appear in either version. The analytical step-size and iteration prescriptions are unchanged; the added theorem hypothesis is a formal assumption change.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, empirical sensitivity analyses, or case studies. Appendix A remains devoted to proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Their expectation and probability bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical numerical results or qualitative experimental findings. Revisions to analytical rate expressions and proof constants are mathematical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4 adds Assumption 1's smoothness and initial-density regularity requirements to Assumption 3. Equation (16) replaces 17/6 with 11/6 in the denominator defining r(d), matching the existing Appendix A.5 derivation. Appendix A.4 normalizes Gamma(t) by 1/N and corrects C_B to C_B T and missing 2d/alpha^2 factors in Lemma 5's estimates. These are local repairs within the retained theorem and proof framework.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same near-optimal KSD rates, Wasserstein convergence with dimension-dependent rates, and long-time propagation-of-chaos contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the bilinear kernel, dimensionality effects, and propagation of chaos are unchanged. Both versions defer analogous discrete-time Wasserstein results to future work.

D1.justification: Algorithm and kernel specifications are retained. Neither version adds implementation details, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: The related-work narrative, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to prior finite-particle and mean-field SVGD theory are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A.3 explicitly names the already-defined density q_K(t) in its introductory sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Section organization and substantive explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Equation spacing and appendix page breaks change locally: the inequality following Gamma(t) moves from page 23 to page 24, with subsequent proof material reflowing across pages 24–26. The introductory schematic is unchanged; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v4 improves internal mathematical consistency: Equation (16) now agrees with Appendix A.5, Theorem 4 explicitly includes regularity needed by its argument, and Lemma 5's normalization and integration factors are corrected. The written hypotheses become more restrictive but more transparent. These targeted repairs support a limited overall improvement while retaining the paper's principal contributions and proof strategy.
